content: Monogenic diabetes should be considered in young patients who present with atypical features of diabetes or have a strong family history of the condition. Genetic testing, particularly for mutations in genes such as HNF1A, HNF4A, and GCK, is often recommended to confirm the diagnosis and guide personalized treatment strategies. Screening for antibodies typically associated with type 1 diabetes can assist in distinguishing monogenic diabetes, especially in cases where the family history does not align with an autoimmune etiology. Health insurance coverage for genetic testing is becoming more widespread, improving accessibility for patients. An accurate diagnosis of monogenic diabetes can help avoid unnecessary insulin therapy, particularly in cases of MODY (Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young) subtypes that can be effectively managed with oral medications.
